subject: Clearance request: VPC/on-prem constraints & audit scope (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clearance request: VPC/on-prem constraints & audit scope (Acme Health)

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our conversation, you confirmed Acme will pursue a Private deployment (VPC) in the EU region with the following non-standard requirements:

- Data residency: all production data must remain in EU region (no cross-border backups).
- Audit rights: Acme requests the ability to perform an audit of systems supporting the Acme tenancy; customer prefers on-site access to logs/config and periodic interviews.
- Deployment constraints: no direct SSH or admin-console access by Redwood staff; any troubleshooting must be via recorded remote session or lift-and-shift artifacts.
- Key management: customer needs HSM integration; they may provide their own HSM or use AWS CloudHSM.
- Commercial ask: 25% first-year discount tied to a 12‑month committed term, and waiver of the one-time professional services (PS) fee.

Attached are the draft SOW and the mutual action plan you shared. We need executive/legal clearance on two things: (1) acceptability of the proposed audit scope (we should avoid unrestricted on-site infrastructure access), and (2) approval for the requested discount and PS waiver.

Please advise quickly — Acme is pushing for signature in the first week of August.

Attachments: redlined_SOW.pdf, MutualActionPlan.xlsx

Best,
Soojin Lee
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-28T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clearance request: VPC/on-prem constraints & audit scope (Acme Health)

Soojin / Rishi —

Quick read of the requested terms. High-level legal take: we can accommodate most items with guarded language, but there are hard stops:

- "On-site access to systems/infra" as requested is too broad. We MUST limit audits to "verification of controls and evidence" (logs, configuration snapshots, policy artifacts). If Acme requires on-site personnel access to our runtime or disk images, we need elevated review and insurance.
- No direct admin/SSH access from Redwood is fine; we should define an approved troubleshooting workflow (recorded remote sessions, timeboxed access via jump host with oversight).
- HSM: integration okay for supported providers. If Acme supplies a customer-controlled HSM on-prem, we need to validate key management interfaces and outline responsibilities.
- Discount: commercial decision, legal needs to add indemnity and data-handling obligations in the SOW for any deviation.

I attached a marked-up set of legal redlines that: (a) narrow the audit clause to evidence-only, (b) add a requirement for 30-day notice for audits, and (c) require that any on-site review exclude source code and runtime debugging sessions.

If sales want to proceed with a deeper concession (25% + PS waived), we need explicit executive approval on the commercial side and signoff that the indemnity exposure is acceptable.

Attachment: legal_redlines.docx

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-29T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clearance request: VPC/on-prem constraints & audit scope (Acme Health)

Team —

Summarizing Acme's position and where I think we can meet them:

- They will buy Dedicated Private (EU) for an initial term that should be at least 12 months. ARR impact is meaningful (estimated ARR $1.2M Y1).
- Must have data residency + HSM integration. They're flexible on provider but want the option to supply their own HSM.
- Audit: they want strong assurances. Per Laura, we should offer a narrowed scope (logs/config snapshots, 30-day notice, remote review).
- Commercial: they asked 25% + PS waived. Given deal economics, I propose we offer 20% first-year discount, PS fee waived if they commit to 12 months, and include the narrowed audit language Laura provided. This keeps net effective price acceptable for the company while securing the contract.

Requesting: Markus — can approve a one-time deviation to standard discount cap (approve 20% deal-level discount for first year only) and confirm PS waiver authority. Laura — confirm you can accept the 30-day-notice evidence-only audit language if we include indemnity and liability caps in the SOW.

Attached: pricing_model.xlsx

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-29T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clearance request: VPC/on-prem constraints & audit scope (Acme Health)

Rishi / team —

Approve 20% first-year discount and waiver of the one-time PS fee under the following conditions:

1) Discount limited to Year 1 only; Year 2+ revert to standard list pricing unless we negotiate renewal.
2) Legal must include indemnity language and liability cap consistent with our enterprise policy.
3) Finance must confirm revenue recognition and implications for the waived PS (we will recognize PS deferral if we need to).
4) Deal must close (signed SOW + payment terms) within 45 days or approval expires.

Provide final redlines and I'll sign off on the deal_id and commercial exceptions.

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Finance (Revenue Ops) | Redwood Inference
